features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Please pass the bread, said Nate. He sat on the dock on a hot summer day. A seal popped up. The seal wanted to ride a sailboat.

You can't ride my boat, Nate said. You are too big. The seal barked and sank down. Nate felt bad. He had a little problem.

He tiptoed to the muddy edge. Come back, he said. I have an idea. He tied a rope to a small raft. The seal climbed on. Nate pulled him slow behind the sailboat.

Then Nate saw the green light. It sat on a bridge over the river. It was far away. It was always far away.

The seal rode and barked. Nate held the rope. He looked at the green light again. It did not come closer. He pulled the raft and watched the green light. The green light stayed on the bridge all day.

stories.name: Nate

features: a little problem that gets solved

stories.text:
Please give Nate a piece of bread. He sits by the river on a hot summer day. A seal pops up. "Hello," says Nate. "Do you want bread?" The seal claps.

A sailboat drifts by. Its sail is torn. "Help!" calls the sailor. Nate wants to help. But the water is muddy. He cannot swim far.

Then Nate sees the green light. It glows on a bridge over the river. The green light is far away. He tiptoes to the edge. The green light pulls him. "Come back," says the seal.

Nate blinks. He ties bread to a stick. The seal takes it to the sailboat. The sailor fixes the sail. "Thank you, Nate!"

The sailboat sails on. The seal dives down. Nate waves. The green light still shines on the bridge. He watches it. He reaches. The green light, the green light, the green light. Always the green light.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Gently, a snowflake landed on Tess's glove. It said, "Hello, I am Pip." Tess laughed. A talking snowflake!

The wind blew hard. It was a windy morning. Tess put Pip in her warm pocket. They went to the woods with her friend Ben.

Ben helped Tess climb a log. The wind made the trees dance. Tess held her glove so Pip would not slide away.

In the dark of the woods, Tess saw a green light. It was far away. It blinked and blinked. Tess wanted to touch the green light. She reached out her hand. The cold made her fingers tingle.

"Come back," said Pip. "The green light is too far."

Ben took Tess's hand. "Let's go home," he said.

Tess looked back one more time. The green light was still there, small and bright. She could not have it. She held Pip close instead.

Pip said, "I am cold too, but I am here with you."

Tess smiled. The green light stayed in the woods, but Tess had her friend and her snowflake.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text: Gently, a snowflake landed on Tess. It said, “Hi, I am Flake.” Tess put out her glove. Flake did not slide off. “I am cold,” Flake said. “But I talk.” Tess and Flake walked in the windy morning. Ben came too. Ben was her friend. He helped her hold Flake safe. Then they saw the green light. It was deep in the dark of the woods. The green light was small and far. Tess wanted the green light. “Do not go,” said Ben. “The woods are dark.” Tess looked at the green light. Then she looked at Flake. Flake said, “Stay with Ben.” Tess felt the cold on her glove. She did not slide away. The green light blinked in the dark of the woods. Tess held Flake close. Ben held her hand. They went home. The green light stayed far behind. Tess still thought of the green light. But Flake was with her. And Ben was too.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Greta the snowflake fell on Tess's glove. "Hello," said Greta. "I can talk."

Tess laughed. "You are just snow."

"No," said Greta. "Watch me slide." She slid to the thumb. "I am special."

They walked in the woods. The wind blew. Tess pulled her coat close. It was cold.

Then Tess saw it. Deep in the dark of the woods, a green light. It was small and far away. It blinked like a tiny star.

"Look," said Tess.

"I see it," said Greta.

Tess ran toward the green light. Her boots sank in the snow. The green light stayed far away.

"Wait," said Ben, her friend. He took her hand. "The path is here."

Tess looked back at the green light. It was still so far. She wanted it. She could not have it.

Greta slid close. "I will stay with you," she said.

Tess smiled. The green light blinked once more. Then the trees hid it.

Ben pulled her glove. "Come home," he said.

So Tess went home. Greta went too. The green light stayed in the woods, far away.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Gently, a snowflake landed on Tess's glove. It said, "Hello." Tess jumped. A talking snowflake! "Do not be scared," it said. "I am just small and cold."

The wind blew hard. Tess held her glove close. "Stay with me," she said. But the snowflake did not stay. It slid off her glove. It slide away on the wind.

Tess ran after it. She went into the dark of the woods. The trees were tall. The wind was loud. She could not see her snowflake friend.

Then she saw a green light. It was far away. It was small and bright. The green light was in the dark of the woods. Tess wanted to hold it. She reached for the green light. She could not get it. It was too far.

Her friend Ben came. He said, "Tess, hold my hand." They walked and walked. The green light stayed far away. It was always far away.

Tess found her snowflake by a rock. "You came back," it said. Tess smiled. But she looked at the green light one more time.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: in the dark of the woods

stories.text:
Gently, a talking snowflake landed on Tess. It said, "Hi, I am Flake." Tess smiled. She put on her warm glove. The wind blew hard.

Then Tess saw the green light. It was far in the dark of the woods. The green light was small and bright.

"I want the green light," Tess said. She began to slide through the snow. The cold bit her nose.

Her friend Ben came. "I will help you," he said. They walked and walked.

But the green light stayed far away. Tess reached out. She could not touch it. The green light just shone.

"The green light is too far," Ben said.

Tess still looked at the green light. The wind blew. The cold grew. She kept walking toward the green light.

"Come back," said Flake. But Tess only saw the green light.

The green light. The green light. She whispered it again and again. Ben held her hand. The green light stayed in the dark of the woods. Tess could not have it.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a tower far away
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Little Nina put the kettle on the stove. She wanted hot milk before bed. The kettle began to hum. Then it began to whistle. Nina liked that sound. She tapped her toes on the floor. Tap, tap, tap.

Out the window, the night was foggy. The moon was soft and far away. On a tower far away, a green light shone. Nina saw the green light. It was small and green in the fog. She looked at the green light. Then she looked back at her kettle.

The kettle whistled more. Nina got her cup. The cup was heavy. She poured the milk. Steam went up like a small cloud. She sat down to drink.

Then the whistle stopped. Nina felt sad. She wanted the sound again. She tapped the kettle. Nothing. She looked out the window. The green light was still there. She could not reach it. She could not make it whistle.

Nina drank her milk. The fog grew thick. The green light went out. The moon hid too. Her kettle was quiet now. Nina smiled a small smile. The quiet was warm. The quiet was good. She did not need the whistle. She did not need the green light. She had her milk.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a tower far away
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Little Nina put the kettle on the stove. The water began to bubble. Soon the kettle would whistle. Nina liked that sound. It made her feel warm inside.

She looked out the window. Fog covered the yard. The moon was soft and far away. Then she saw it. On a tower far away, a green light glowed. The green light blinked in the fog. Nina wanted to touch it. She tapped the glass. The green light did not come closer.

The kettle whistled. Nina ran to the stove. She made her tea. Then she went back to the window. The green light was still there. It looked like a tiny star. She wished she could hold it. Her tea grew cold.

She heard a heavy knock at the door. It was her friend Sam. Sam brought cookies. They sat and ate. Nina told Sam about the green light. Sam smiled.

“That is just the lighthouse,” Sam said. “It keeps boats safe.”

Nina looked again. The green light was not a star. It was a helper. She still liked it. She waved good night to the green light. Then she drank her tea.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a tower far away
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Little Nina put the kettle on the stove. She wanted warm milk before bed. The kettle began to hum. Then it began to whistle.

Nina looked out the window. It was a foggy night. The moon was soft and white. Far away, on a tall tower, she saw the green light. It blinked and blinked. The green light looked warm. Nina wanted to hold it.

She tapped the window with one finger. The green light did not come closer. The fog was heavy. It wrapped the tower like a blanket.

The kettle whistled louder. Nina turned back to the stove. She poured the milk. Then she looked out again. The green light was still there. She reached for it with her hand. Her hand touched cold glass.

The kettle stopped whistling. The house was quiet. Nina held her warm cup. She thought about the green light. She thought about it a lot.

Then she heard a small sound. The kettle was whistling again. But Nina had not turned on the stove. She smiled. Maybe the green light was calling her after all.

stories.name: Nina

features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Little Nina filled the kettle and put it on the stove. Soon it began to whistle. The sound was soft at first, then loud. Nina liked the whistle. It meant tea time.

Outside, fog wrapped the house. Nina looked out the window. Far away, on a tower, she saw a small green light. It blinked in the fog. Nina forgot the kettle. She wanted the green light.

The kettle whistled louder. Nina did not hear it. She thought only of the green light. Green light, green light, green light. She tapped the glass with one finger.

The moon was hidden. The fog was heavy. The kettle screamed on the stove, but Nina stared at the green light. She reached for it. Her hand touched cold glass. The green light stayed far away.

Then a small twist. The green light went out. Just like that. Nina blinked. She heard the kettle again. She ran and turned off the stove.

She made her tea. It was warm. The green light was gone. But Nina knew it would come back. It always came back. She sipped her tea and waited.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a tower far away
features: a small twist near the end

stories.text:
Little Nina put the kettle on the stove. She waited for it to sing. The night was foggy and soft.

Then she saw it. On a tower far away, a green light glowed. The fog could not hide the green light. Nina forgot the kettle.

She went to the window. The green light was so small. She wanted to hold it. She tapped the glass. The green light did not move.

The kettle began to whistle. Nina did not hear it. She only saw the green light. Green light. Green light. Her heart said green light.

The moon was heavy and white. It hung in the fog. Nina reached out. Her hand found only cold air. The green light stayed far away.

The kettle whistled and whistled. Then it stopped. Nina turned at last. The water was gone. The kettle was dry and hot.

She touched the spout. It was not hot at all. The stove was never on. The kettle had whistled by itself, all for the green light.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Before bed, Nina found a magic ice cream cone in her pocket. It never melted. She could lick it and wish for one small thing. She wished for a boat to ride on the lake.

That foggy night, she took her boat out. The fog was soft and gray. She could not see far. Then she saw a green light, far across the water. It was small and bright. She wanted to touch it. She tried to row to it. But the green light stayed far away. She rowed and rowed. Her arms got tired.

She had to run home before morning. Her magic cone was gone. She had used her one wish on the boat. She sat by the window and looked out. The green light was still there, across the lake. She could see it but never reach it. Some pretty things stay far away. That made her sad.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Bella Nina found a magic ice cream cone. It never melted. It stayed cold and sweet in her pocket all day.

Nina went to the lake. Fog sat on the water like a wet blanket. A small boat rocked far out. On the boat, a green light glowed.

She wanted to run to it. But the water was deep and dark. The green light was so soft and far. It called to her.

She held her ice cream cone. It was magic, but it could not help her swim. She stood on the shore. The fog grew thick. The green light stayed on the boat. It always stayed just out of reach.

Nina ate her cone. It tasted like nothing now. She sat down on the cold sand. The green light blinked once, then the fog hid it.

She never got to the boat. She never touched the green light. Some things you can see, but you can never have. That is the sad truth.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Bella the ice cream cone was magic. Nina found it in her pocket. It was cold and sweet. If you licked it, you could hear the sea.

Nina took it everywhere. She held it in her hand. The magic made her happy.

One foggy night, she went to the lake. A boat sat out on the water. A green light shone on the boat. It was far away. It was very soft.

Nina wanted to reach the green light. She put the cone in her pocket. She began to run. But the boat was too far.

She looked at the green light. It called to her. The ice cream melted in her pocket. She forgot to eat it. The green light was all she saw.

The fog grew thick. The boat drifted away. The green light grew small. Then it was gone.

Nina sat down. Her pocket was empty. The magic was gone too. She had lost the sweet cone for a light she could not touch. Sometimes we chase what we cannot have and lose what we love.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Best of all, Nina had a magic ice cream cone. It never melted. It never ran out. She put it in her pocket and felt happy.

But then the fog came. Soft and gray. It covered the lake. Nina saw a boat out on the water. On the boat was a green light. It was small and bright. It was far away.

“Come,” said the green light. “Come here.”

Nina wanted to run to it. She wanted to hold it. She forgot her ice cream cone. She forgot her warm bed.

She walked to the water. The green light moved away. She walked more. The green light stayed far. Always far.

Her magic ice cream cone fell from her pocket. It sank in the dark water. She did not see. She only saw the green light.

The boat drifted away. The green light grew small. Then it was gone.

Nina stood alone in the fog. She reached and reached.

If you chase what you cannot hold, you lose what you already have.

stories.name: Nina

axes.where: on a boat out on the lake

stories.text:
Bella Nina found a magic ice cream cone. It never melted. It tasted like stars.

Nina put it in her pocket. She wanted to show her mom. But then she saw the green light.

The green light was on a boat out on the lake. The fog was thick. The night was dark. The green light was soft and far.

Nina began to run. She ran to the water. She forgot the ice cream cone. She forgot her mom.

The boat rocked. The green light stayed far away. Nina reached and reached.

"Green light," she whispered. "Green light, green light."

Her pocket felt empty. The cone was gone. The green light was still there, soft on the foggy lake.

Nina stood alone. She never reached the green light. She never found the cone.

Some things we want most are the things we cannot hold.

stories.name: Leo

axes.where: on a little island

stories.text:
A boy named Leo loved the playground slide. It was shiny and tall. He climbed up, up, up and slid down fast. Whee!

On a sunny afternoon, Leo ate a red apple. He sat on the grass. Then he saw something far away. A little green light shone on a little island. It was a green light, small and bright. Leo wanted it. He did not know why.

He stood on his tiptoes. He reached out. The green light stayed far away. Leo's shoes got muddy in the grass. He slipped and fell on his bottom. Plop! He laughed and laughed.

A duck quacked at him. His mom called him back.

Leo climbed the slide again. He slid down and forgot the green light. The green light was pretty, but it was not for him. Some lights are just to look at, not to hold.

stories.name: Leo

axes.where: on a little island

stories.text:
A shiny slide stood in the playground. Leo ran to it on a sunny afternoon. He climbed up and slid down fast. Whee! He did it again and again.

Then Leo saw a green light. It was far away on a little island. The green light was small and bright. Leo wanted to touch it. He tiptoed to the fence. He could not reach the green light.

Leo sat down and ate a red apple. He was muddy from the slide. A bird flew by and dropped a leaf on his head. Leo laughed. That was funny!

He looked up. The green light was still there. It blinked on the little island. Leo waved at the green light. The green light did not wave back.

He climbed the slide again. Down he went, happy and muddy. The green light stayed far away. Leo smiled anyway.

You cannot always reach what you want. But you can still have fun where you are.

stories.text: A boy named Leo loved the playground slide. It was shiny and tall. He liked to climb up and zoom down. On a sunny afternoon, Leo found a muddy puddle near the slide. He did not want to get his shoes dirty. So he took a big tiptoe step. Plop! He slipped on a squishy apple someone dropped. His bottom went right in the mud. Leo laughed so hard his tummy hurt. Then he saw something far away. A green light glowed on a little island across the water. It was small and bright. Leo wanted to touch it. He reached out his hand. The green light stayed far away. He climbed the slide to see it better. Down he went, but the green light did not come closer. Again and again, he looked at the green light on the little island. It was pretty and soft. But he could not have it. At last, Leo sat on the slide and smiled. Some things are lovely just to look at, even if you cannot hold them.

stories.name: Leo

stories.text:
A sunny afternoon was perfect for the playground slide. Leo climbed the ladder. He went down fast. He laughed. Then he saw it.

On a little island in the pond, a green light glowed. It was small and bright. Leo wanted it.

He took his apple and put it in his pocket. He tried to tiptoe to the water. His shoes got muddy. Splash! He slipped and sat down hard. A duck quacked at him. That was funny.

The green light stayed on the little island. Leo reached for the green light. He could not touch it.

He went back to the slide. Down he went. But his eyes found the green light again. It shone on the little island. He reached. He could not have it.

The green light kept calling him.

Some things are pretty to see. But you cannot always have them. And that is okay.

stories.name: Leo

A sunny afternoon was perfect for the playground slide. Leo climbed the ladder. He went down fast. He went down slow. He laughed. Then he saw the green light.

It was on a little island, far away. The green light sat on the sand. Leo wanted the green light. He tiptoed to the edge of the grass. The green light was still far.

He found a muddy apple in his pocket. He held it out. Maybe the green light wanted it. The green light did not move.

He tiptoed to a log. He tiptoed to a rock. The green light stayed on the little island. Leo reached and reached. The green light was so close and so far.

He slipped on the muddy grass. Plop! He sat in a puddle. That was funny. He laughed at his muddy shoes.

The green light blinked once. Then it was gone.

Leo went back to the slide. Some lights are just for looking, not for having.

stories.name: June

axes.where: on a car parked far down the street

stories.text: When June went fishing, she found a boot in the water. It was old and brown and full of mud. June pulled it up with a loud splash. She put it on a chair to dry. Her friend May came to help. "That is a funny fish," May said. They both laughed. June wanted to find the other boot. She looked in the foggy water. Then she saw a green light. It was on a car parked far down the street. The green light was small and far away. June wanted to hop over and touch it. But the car was too far. May said, "Let's go home." June looked at the green light one more time. It blinked in the fog. She could not reach it. She picked up her boot and walked away. The green light stayed far down the street. June did not look back.

stories.name: June

stories.text:
When June went fishing, she sat on a chair by the water. She wanted a big fish. She did not want a boot. Then she felt a pull. It was heavy. It was a boot! June was sad.

Her friend Lee said, "Do not be sad. Let us hop home." They walked in the fog. It was a foggy night. The street was very quiet.

Then June saw a green light. It was on a car far down the street. The green light was small and soft. June wanted to touch it. "Come on," said Lee. But June looked at the green light. She took one step. The green light was too far.

A loud sound came. A dog barked. June jumped. Lee held her hand. "The green light is far," Lee said. "We can not get it."

June looked back. The green light was still there. It was so pretty. She wanted it. But she could not have it. She went home with Lee. She did not get the green light. But she had her friend. That was good.

stories.name: June

stories.text:
Waves washed the old boot to June's boat. She was a fisherman. She pulled the boot from the water. It was brown and wet. "A boot," June said. "Not a fish."

Her friend Ben rowed close. "Throw it back," he said.

"No," said June. "I will keep it."

That night, fog sat on the sea. June tied her boat and walked home. Everything was soft and gray. She saw a green light on a car parked far down the street. The green light was small and bright. June stopped. She wanted to touch it.

"Come on," said Ben.

June took a hop. Then she took a step. The green light called her down the street. Her boot was heavy in her hand. The fog made the green light blur. Ben held her arm. "It is just a lamp on a car," he said.

June sat on a chair by the window. She could still see the green light. It was far away. It was so far. She reached out her hand. The green light did not come. It never would. But the green light still shone. And June still looked.

stories.name: June

stories.text: When June the fisherman pulled up a wet boot, she laughed. It was old and brown. She put it on her chair. Then she saw it. Far down the street, on a car, sat a small green light. Fog made it soft. June did a hop. "Look," she said. Her friend May looked too. "It is just a green light," May said. But June wanted it. The green light blinked. It was so far. June took a step. Then ten. May held her arm. "Stay," May said. A loud dog barked. June did not stop. The green light glowed. It pulled her like a fish on a line. May pulled her back. The green light stayed on the car. It would not come. June reached. Her hand was empty. Fog ate the street. The boot sat on the chair at home. The green light sat on the car, far away. June could not have it. Not that night. Not ever. Good night, green light.

stories.text:
When June went fishing, she pulled up a boot. It was old and brown. Her friend May said, "That is not a fish." June put the boot on a chair. Then she saw the green light.

The green light was on a car far down the street. Fog hid the car. The green light was small and bright. June wanted it. She did not want the boot.

"Let's hop," said May. "Let's go home." But June did not hop. She walked to the green light. The fog was loud and wet. May held her hand.

The green light was far. The green light was always far. June reached. She could not touch it. The green light stayed on the car.

May said, "Come back to the chair." June did not come. She looked at the green light. The green light looked back. The green light was the only thing.

June said, "Green light." She said it soft. She said it loud. The green light did not move. June did not move. The boot was gone. May was gone. Only the green light was there. June reached. June could not have it. The green light was far. The green light was always far.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: on the other side of a fence

stories.text:
In the morning, Tess went to see her friend Ben. Ben tells the best jokes. He makes her laugh so much her tummy hurts.

"Knock, knock," said Ben.

"Who is there?" said Tess.

"Snow," said Ben.

"Snow who?" said Tess.

"Snow use staying inside. Let's go out!" Ben said. Tess laughed.

They went out. It was windy. Tess stepped in a puddle. Splash! Her feet got wet.

Ben told a joke about a wet sock. Tess giggled. Then she saw something. Past the fence, far away, was a green light. It was small and bright. It glowed in the gray morning.

Tess held the fence and looked. The green light seemed to call her. She wanted to climb the fence. But it was too high.

"Come on," said Ben. "I know a joke about a fence."

Tess turned back. Ben's joke was funny. The green light stayed behind the fence. Tess did not reach it. But she had her friend, and that was good.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: on the other side of a fence

stories.text:
I like my friend Ben. Ben tells jokes. He tells a joke about a duck. He tells a joke about a sock. I laugh and laugh.

One early morning we walk to the field. The grass is wet. There is a puddle on the path. We jump over it.

"Knock knock," says Ben.

"Who is there?" I say.

"Worm," says Ben. "Worm who?"

I do not know. Ben laughs.

Then I see it. Past the fence, far away, a green light shines. It is small and soft. It is a green light in the gray morning. I want to climb the fence and go to it. But I stay.

It is windy. Ben tells a joke about the wind. I laugh, but I look back. The green light is still there.

"Are you okay?" says Ben.

"Yes," I say. "Tell me one more joke."

Ben tells a joke about a frog. The green light glows past the fence. I hear Ben laughing. I hold his hand. The green light stays far away, but Ben is here.

stories.name: Tess

axes.where: on the other side of a fence

stories.text:
In the morning Tess went to see her friend Jo. Jo tells jokes. Jo says, "Why did the puddle say hi? It was in a good mood!" Tess laughed.

Then Tess saw the green light. It was on the other side of a fence. The green light was small and far away. It shone in the windy air.

"Look, Jo," said Tess. "The green light."

"I see a puddle," said Jo. "Why did the puddle stop? It ran out of rain!"

Tess did not laugh. She held the fence. She wanted to climb the fence. She wanted to touch the green light.

"Come back," said Jo. "I have a joke. Why did the cloud hide? It was shy!"

The green light stayed far away. Tess climbed one step. The wind blew. The green light did not come closer.

"One more joke," said Jo. "Why is the sky so high? So the green light can hide!"

Tess looked at Jo. She smiled a little. But her eyes went back to the green light, on the other side of the fence, in the windy early morning.

stories.name: Tess

stories.text:
In the morning Tess went to see her friend Ben. Ben tells jokes. He tells jokes all day.

"Knock knock," said Ben.

"Who is there?" said Tess.

"A windy cow," said Ben. "Moo-ve over!"

Tess did not laugh. She looked past Ben. She saw the fence. She saw the green light on the other side of the fence.

"Ben," said Tess. "Do you see the green light?"

"What green light?" said Ben. "Listen. Why did the puddle cross the road?"

Tess did not hear him. She walked to the fence. The green light was small and far. It was on the other side of the fence.

She tried to climb the fence. The fence was too high.

"Tess," said Ben. "Want a joke?"

The green light blinked. Tess put her hands on the fence.

"Why did the chicken sit on a puddle?" said Ben.

The green light was still there. Tess did not climb. She did not laugh. She only looked at the green light.

"Good joke," said Tess. But she did not turn around.

stories.text:
I like my friend Tess. Tess tells jokes. She says, "Why did the boy sit on the clock? He wanted to be on time!" I laugh.

Tess walks to the fence. The grass is wet. There is a puddle by her feet. The morning is windy and cold.

"Look," says Tess.

On the other side of the fence is a green light. It is small and far. Tess holds the fence. She wants to climb it.

"Come back," I say. "Tell me a joke."

"The green light," says Tess. "I want to touch it."

She puts her hands on the fence. She does not climb. She looks at the green light. The green light is so far. The green light is so small.

"Tell me a joke," I say again.

"Green light," says Tess. "Green light, green light."

The wind blows. The puddle moves. Tess holds the fence. She looks at the green light. She never looks away. The green light. The green light. The green light.

stories.topic: A plane and a paper kite
stories.name: Ravi

axes.where: at the very top of a tall tree

stories.text: One cold autumn evening, Ravi made a paper kite. He wanted it to fly like a plane. His friend Mira helped him tie the string. They ran to the park. The wind blew hard. The kite went up, up, up. Then it got stuck at the very top of a tall tree. Ravi felt shy. He did not want to climb. Mira laughed. “You look like a bear with a brush!” she said. That was funny. Ravi laughed too. He gave the string a little tug. The kite did a skip in the air. Then it stayed. Ravi saw a small green light high in the branches. It was just the evening star. He wished he could touch it. He reached up. He could not. Mira helped him pull the kite free. It came down with a happy flop. They walked home. The green light stayed far away. Ravi waved good night to it.

stories.text:
On a cold autumn evening, Ravi took his paper kite to the hill. His friend Mira came too. She held the string while he ran.

The wind was shy. It came and went. The kite dipped low, then jumped up high. Ravi laughed. A plane flew far above them, loud and silver. “Look!” said Mira. “It flies better than us.”

Ravi tried to brush the grass off his knees. He wanted to skip home, but the kite tugged. It climbed and climbed. Then it stopped. It was stuck at the very top of a tall tree.

“Oh no,” said Ravi.

Mira pulled the string. Nothing. She shook the tree. A leaf fell on her nose. They both laughed.

Then Ravi saw it. A small green light blinked at the top of the tree. The green light sat among the branches, calm and far. He wanted it. He reached up. His hand closed on cold air.

“Come on,” said Mira. “We can try tomorrow.”

Ravi looked back once. The green light still blinked. He walked home slow, thinking of the green light.

Mira said, "Ravi, hold the string!"

He did not hear her. Green light, green light. He wanted it so much.

Mira used a brush to tap his arm. "Wake up!"

Ravi blinked. The green light stayed in the tree. He could not have it. He held the string again. The kite flew, small and red, under the cold sky.

Little Kai found a kitten in the snow. The kitten had soft wings. They were white like the snow. Kai named her Fluff.

Fluff could not fly yet. She tried to flutter up. She fell in a soft pile. Kai laughed. He helped her up.

Kai used a brush on her wings. He made them neat. Fluff gave a wiggle. Her tail was curly. She was warm now.

They played in the yard. Fluff hopped and skipped. Kai threw a small snowball. Fluff chased it.

Then Kai saw a green light. It was far across the snowy yard. It blinked once. It blinked twice. It felt warm and kind. Kai wanted to go to the green light. But his boots were wet. And Fluff was cold.

The green light faded away. Kai picked up Fluff. He went inside.

The small twist was this. The green light was not a light at all. It was the sun on a window. It was just a window of a house. But Kai did not know. He only knew he wished he could reach it someday.

Little Kai found a kitten in the snow. The kitten had wings. They were soft and white. Kai wrapped it in a scarf.

The kitten gave a tiny wiggle. Its wings went flutter, flutter. Kai tried to brush off the snow. The wings were so curly at the tips.

Then Kai saw the green light. It was across the snowy yard. It blinked under a pine tree. The green light looked warm.

Kai held the kitten close. They walked toward the green light. The snow went crunch, crunch. The green light stayed far away.

The kitten sneezed. It flew up fast. It did a loop and landed on Kai's head. Kai laughed.

Again the green light glowed across the yard. Kai took one more step. The light moved farther. It always did.

Kai stopped. The kitten licked Kai's nose. Kai turned around and went home. The green light kept shining behind them.

He gave his wings a wiggle. Then he took his brush and cleaned them. He pushed the door open. Cold snow hit his nose.

He ran and ran. The green light stayed far. He jumped. He flapped. He fell in the snow.

The green light did not come closer. Kai felt sad. Then he saw something. The green light was not far at all.

It was the shiny tag on his own collar. It bounced when he ran. It glowed in the snow.

Kai laughed. He wiggled his curly wings. He walked back home. The green light went with him.

He pushed the door. The cold air made him sneeze. He saw the yard. It was all white. Then he saw the green light. It was across the snowy yard.

The green light was far away. Kai flapped his wings. He wanted to reach the green light. He took a step. The snow was deep. He tried to brush it with his paw.

The green light stayed far. Kai did a wiggle. He jumped. His wings went flutter. But the green light did not come closer.

He ran and ran. The snow was soft. His fur got curly from the wet. Still the green light was far. Always far.

Kai sat down. He was tired. He looked at the green light. It was pretty. It was always there. He could not touch it. He could not reach it.

Then he heard a sound. A small bird sat on the fence. The bird had a tiny green light on its head. It was a firefly. The green light was a bug. Kai laughed.

He went back inside. The green light was still out there. But Kai was warm now.

axes.where: deep at the bottom of a pond

stories.text: Sometimes a cake has no candles. Eli helped Grandma make one. It was round and warm. It smelled like sweet bananas. "Where are the candles?" Eli asked. Grandma said, "We ate them all." That was a funny joke. Eli laughed so hard his tummy hurt. He carried a bucket of berries to the table. He did a little spin. He wore his fuzzy blue socks. Then he slid on the floor. "Whoa!" he said. Grandma caught him. They ate cake with no candles. It was just before bedtime. Eli felt happy and full. Later he looked out the window. Far away, deep at the bottom of a pond, he saw the green light. It sat there like a tiny star in the water. He wanted to touch it. He could not. The green light stayed where it was. It was time for bed. Eli yawned. He thought of cake and berries. He did not think of the green light again.

Sitting at the table, Eli looked at his cake. It had no candles. Not one. Tomorrow he would be six, but tonight the cake just sat there, round and bare.

"Maybe we forgot the candles," said Mom.

"Maybe the cake is shy," said Dad.

Eli laughed. That was funny.

Then he saw the green light. It was deep at the bottom of the pond outside the window. The green light was small and far away. It glowed under the dark water.

Eli wanted it. He took his bucket and walked to the pond. He reached in, but the green light stayed deep.

"I can get it," he said.

He tried to spin the bucket like a net. The water went splash. His socks got wet and fuzzy. Mom called him inside.

"No candles," she said. "Time for bed."

Eli climbed under the covers. He thought of the green light. He wanted the green light. He could not have the green light.

Soon his eyes grew heavy. The green light blinked once, far away, and then he slept.

He carried his plate to the window. Just before bedtime, the yard was dark. Down past the fence was the pond. Deep at the bottom of the pond, the green light was waiting. It always waited.

Eli put down his fork. He took his bucket to the pond. He leaned over the water. "I see you, green light," he said. The green light did not come up. It never came up.

He tried to scoop it. The bucket came back with one fuzzy leaf and a very surprised frog. The frog jumped on his nose. Eli laughed so hard he sat down.

Then he looked again. The green light was still there. Deep and small and far.

"Please," he whispered. The green light only shone.

Eli went back inside. He ate his cake in the dark. The green light stayed in the pond. He could not have it. He wished he could spin it into his hand. But he could not. So he wished it good night.

“Green light,” Eli whispered. “Green light, come here.”

His mom called him for bed. Eli looked back. The green light stayed in the pond. He could not have it. He went inside, and the cake still had no candles.

Next to the sofa, Kai did a puzzle. It was a big puzzle with a boat and a whale. One piece was missing. Kai looked under the rug. He looked in his sock drawer. No piece.

Kai took his kite to the sunny hill. The wind pulled it high. Far away, high up on a mountain, he saw a green light. It blinked once, small and far. Kai blinked too.

He walked home. His mom smiled. "Look in your pocket," she said. Kai felt his coat pocket. There it was! The missing piece was small and round.

Kai put it in the puzzle. Click! The boat was whole. The whale was whole. Kai felt proud. He ran outside and let his kite sing in the wind. The green light stayed on the mountain, far away, but Kai did not need it. His puzzle was done. He was happy.

Kai sat on the floor. The puzzle showed a big blue lake. One spot stayed empty, right in the middle. It made him sad.

He went outside to fly his kite. The sun was warm. The kite went up, up, up. Kai felt proud.

Then he saw it. High up on a mountain, far away, a little green light was shining. The green light sat on the peak like a tiny star. Kai could see the green light, but he could not reach it.

He wanted the green light. He wished he could hold it.

His mom called him in. She held up a small piece. "It was in your coat!"

Kai laughed. He put the piece in the puzzle. The lake was whole. He did not need the green light. He began to sing.

Then Kai saw a green light. It was high up on a mountain. The green light blinked in the sunny afternoon. It was far away. Kai could not reach it. He felt a little sad.

He went outside to fly his kite. The kite went up, up, up. It danced near the clouds. Kai did not sing. He kept looking at the green light on the mountain. The green light was so pretty. He wished he could touch it. But the green light stayed far away.

His friend Mia came by. She held up a small blue piece. "I found it!" she said.

Kai was so proud. He put the piece in the puzzle. The sky was done. He sang a happy song. The green light was still on the mountain. But now Kai did not mind.
